chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Lucky Millinder's band: personnel and constant firing
summary: Millinder replaced Jackson with white trombonists Freddie Zito and Porky Cohen; Jackson lists the band, and Bullmoose Jackson said he played with a hundred saxophonists.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: -- so, anyway, I went with Lucky and he fired me and he took Gene Simon back. He fired me and hired two white trombone players. Yeah, Freddie Zito -- and a dear friend of mine, too, Freddie is. We worked in the house band at the Waldorf together. And Porky Cohen was a very dear friend of mine. Porky Cohen was the only white trombone player I knew that could play the plunger. He played the plunger with Charlie Barnet when Charlie used to play Duke's arrangements, and Porky Cohen was the plunger. He played the plunger. He was a very good trombone player.
And the trumpets? He had -- Lucky had in the trumpets, he had Nottingham, he had Reynauld Jones, had Joe Wilder, and Frank Galbreath. That was the trumpets.
And the trombones was Al Gray and myself and Gene Simon, you see? And I can't --
The reeds? Heads Adams. He's from Buffalo, I think.
Yeah, Heads Adams. What a name.
Yeah. And the singer, the great vocalist at that time, Bullmoose Jackson.

Bullmoose Jackson was in that saxophone section. Billy Mitchell was in that saxophone section. But I can't think of the rhythm section. I just can't think of them. There was two brothers, one a pianist and one a bass player. And the one that was a bass player turned out to be an organist around Detroit. And the drummer I forget. I've seen the drummer around now, every now and then, and I forget his name, too.

But it was a good band, a good band, and Lucky -- Bullmoose told me a lot of times Lucky fired so many guys that, he said, for the time he was there he had played with about a hundred different saxophone players. He said sometimes he
would come to work at night and he didn't know who was going to be sitting there.
But even after he fired me and Gene, he took Gene Simon back and had him as a road manager.
That's the kind of guy Lucky was.
